capital.note: patient capital with low holding costs

meta.note: Three criteria are hard filters; the rest are weighted and combined into the 0-100 Buyer-Fit score. The buyer's low holding cost is context, not a filter - it is why patience through the 2027 soft patch is affordable.

criteria.d: Confirmed per-listing via Landgate cadastre - no public source publishes median block size.
Suburb median used as a proxy; in-band or just-below scores highest; a soft ceiling (listing prices are estimates), only well above ~$1.1M is heavily penalised.
Low holding costs make patience cheap. Not a filter - the reason waiting is affordable.
Scarce land, school zones and undersupply favoured.
Demographics, parks, school quality, childcare pressure.
Larger blocks, lower unit density, original stock, pool-permit rate.
4+ achievable; a knock-down-rebuild can satisfy this.
Old is fine where land value exceeds improved value (KDR economics).
School catchment, median level and amenity as proxies.
